Arm the target to wait out a usage limit and carry on

Usage:
  cmux rate-limit-options

Sends /rate-limit-options, which opens Claude Code's own menu for what to do
when you hit a usage limit.

Arming the auto-resume option there is the reliable way to stop a session
stalling overnight: it waits for the limit to reset and continues by itself,
with no watching and no screen scraping. Prefer it over cmux watch, which
exists only for sessions that reached the limit without being armed.

Example:
  cmux --to %12 rate-limit-options

Flags:
  --to <target>      pane id (%12), session:window.pane, or an index from cmux panes
  --all-panes        allow a target that was not detected as Claude Code
  --dry-run          print the tmux calls instead of making them
  --defer <seconds>  have tmux deliver the keys later, via run-shell
  --self             allow interrupt to target the pane cmux was run from
  -h, --help         show help
  --version          show version
